papers.title_en: GeoTrain: Energy-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Foundation Model Training on Heterogeneous Geo-Distributed Resources
papers.authors: Bui-Khanh Hoang, TianZhang He, Mohammad Goudarzi
papers.evidence: 面向异构地理分布式训练集群的自动并行配置
papers.tldr: 前沿基础模型训练通常依赖集中式高速集群，成本高且只有资源充足机构可负担。GeoTrain 面向异构地理分布式 GPU，联合选择 GPU、划分模型层并确定流水线配置，同时考虑算力、内存、功耗和网络约束。它用带专用遗传算子与局部搜索的模因算法探索大组合空间。在真实与模拟拓扑上，迭代时间和能耗分别最多降低 61.4% 与 11.7%，并能暴露更优的能效-时间权衡。
papers.abstract_en: Training foundation models at the frontier typically requires large-scale dedicated and centralized clusters with fast interconnects - infrastructure that is prohibitively expensive and generally accessible only to well-resourced organizations. Decentralized training over pooled, geographically distributed GPUs offers an alternative, but introduces substantial heterogeneity in compute, memory, power, and network performance. Existing distributed training systems are primarily designed for clusters with fast, low-latency interconnects and typically use all available GPUs when configuring parallel training. In geo-distributed environments, however, slower devices and weak network links can become bottlenecks, while optimizing solely for throughput overlooks significant energy cost.   We present GeoTrain, an automatic parallelism system that jointly optimizes training performance and energy consumption for heterogeneous geo-distributed GPU environments. GeoTrain simultaneously selects GPUs, partitions model layers, and determines pipeline configurations while accounting for heterogeneous compute, memory, power, and network constraints. To efficiently explore this large combinatorial search space, GeoTrain employs an optimized memetic algorithm with specialized genetic operators and local search. Experiments with decoder-only Transformer models on real-world and simulated heterogeneous topologies demonstrate that GeoTrain reduces iteration time and energy consumption by up to $61.4\%$ and $11.7\%$, respectively, over the existing state-of-the-art approaches. It also finds the exact optimum on verifiable instances and scales beyond exact methods as the number of GPUs increases, while exposing favorable energy-time trade-offs, including cases where its time-optimal distributed training plan is both faster and more energy-efficient than the baselines.

papers.title_en: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
papers.authors: Haotian Zheng, Zhanwei Wang, Kaibin Huang
papers.evidence: 专家激活偏斜导致分布式MoE专家间计算功耗不均
papers.tldr: 空间数据中心承载大模型推理时，MoE专家激活偏斜会造成卫星间算力功耗供需不均，活跃专家受限而空闲专家太阳能未充分利用。为此提出SpaceWPT框架，利用星间激光无线传能重新分配采集功率，并推导简化控制的设计原则与平均时延代理模型。进一步给出按水位和链路效率决定捐赠、保留或接收功率的双侧注水策略。仿真显示Mixtral-8x7B与Phi-3.5-MoE推理时延最多降低29.25%，紧凑编队和高传能效率下收益更大。
papers.abstract_en: Space data centers (SpaceDCs) are emerging as platforms for large language models (LLMs), supported by continuous solar-energy harvesting and high-speed interconnections. The mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture supports distributed LLM inference by deploying experts across satellites. However, skewed expert activation creates uneven computation power demands despite uniform solar-power supply at the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit (SSO). Consequently, active experts remain power-constrained while harvested power at idle experts is underused. These reduce inference efficiency and increase latency. To address this supply-demand mismatch, we propose the SpaceWPT framework, which uses inter-satellite laser-based wireless power transfer (WPT) to redistribute harvested power. The key design challenge is to balance the computation demands of power-donating and power-receiving satellites under WPT losses: transferring more power accelerates computation at the receiver but leaves less power for the donor. After deriving design principles that simplify WPT control, we characterize the resulting latency tradeoff through a tractable surrogate of average inference latency. Minimizing the surrogate yields a novel two-sided water-filling strategy that determines whether each active expert donates, retains, or receives power according to the water level and its WPT link efficiency. Simulations with Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE show up to 29.25% lower inference latency than without WPT, with larger gains under more compact formations and higher transfer efficiencies.
